newsitem.title: TAIWAN: FIRST COMMERCIAL RAISES PRIME RATE TO 7.65 PCT.
newsitem.headline: FIRST COMMERCIAL RAISES PRIME RATE TO 7.65 PCT.

text.p: First Commercial Bank, one of Taiwan's "Big Three" state-run banks, said on Thursday it was raising its prime lending rate by 0.125 percentage point to 7.65 percent, effective Friday.
The bank also was raising its one-month-to-three-year time deposits rates by between 0.05 and 0.20 percentage point.
The bank was taking cue from the Bank of Taiwan and Cooperative Bank of Taiwan, which raised their interest rates on Thursday.
Various private commercial banks also raised rates.
The rate hikes came nearly a week after the central bank's decision to increase two key interest rates to stabilise the foreign exchange market.
Central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong said on July 31 the bank was raising the rediscount rate and accommodations against secured loans to 5.25 and 5.625 percent, respectively, effective August 1.
